subject: System Design
title: The Therac-25 Radiation Overdoses
description: A quick, practical guide to The Therac-25 Radiation Overdoses.

hook.text: Between 1985 and 1987, a radiation therapy machine gave patients 100x the intended dose. Six were injured, three died.

buildup.text: The Therac-25 removed hardware safety interlocks, relying solely on software for safety checks.

discovery.text: A race condition in the control software allowed the high-energy beam to fire without the safety filter.

twist.text: The bug only triggered when a fast typist edited the treatment plan in a specific sequence — hard to reproduce.

climax.text: Life-critical software must be verified with extraordinary rigor. Therac-25 proved the cost of failure.

punchline.text: A race condition in medical software cost lives.

quiz.question: What design flaw made Therac-25 dangerous?
options: It removed hardware safety interlocks, relying only on software
It used the wrong radiation type
